source.title: Independence of ℓ for Frobenius conjugacy classes attached to abelian varieties
source.version: 63-page revised preprint of7 October2024; final Annals revision of19 November2024 not compared
readSections: All§6:Mumford–Tate realization and rational representative refinement

summary: Kisin and Zhou prove that for an abelian variety A over a number field and a prime v | p > 2 of good reduction, the ℓ-adic Frobenius conjugacy classes in the Mumford–Tate group G come from a single rational class γ ∈ Conj_G(Q), for all ℓ ≠ p (Theorem 1.1). They do this through integral models of Shimura varieties of Hodge type for strongly acceptable triples at very special parahoric level. The μ-ordinary locus is open and dense and its points lift to special points (Theorem 1.3), and curves through Kottwitz–Rapoport strata over the same residue field with Chin's companions give ℓ-independence at every mod p point (Theorem 1.2). Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and fourteen findings are recorded; the proof gaps E10–E12 and E14 have repairs and the rest are misprints. Not formalised.

structure DividedPowers where
  /-- The divided power function underlying a divided power structure -/
  dpow : ℕ → A → A
  dpow_null : ∀ {n x} (_ : x ∉ I), dpow n x = 0
  dpow_zero : ∀ {x} (_ : x ∈ I), dpow 0 x = 1
  dpow_one : ∀ {x} (_ : x ∈ I), dpow 1 x = x
  dpow_mem : ∀ {n x} (_ : n ≠ 0) (_ : x ∈ I), dpow n x ∈ I
  dpow_add : ∀ {n} {x y} (_ : x ∈ I) (_ : y ∈ I),
    dpow n (x + y) = (antidiagonal n).sum fun k ↦ dpow k.1 x * dpow k.2 y
  dpow_mul : ∀ {n} {a : A} {x} (_ : x ∈ I),
    dpow n (a * x) = a ^ n * dpow n x
  mul_dpow : ∀ {m n} {x} (_ : x ∈ I),
    dpow m x * dpow n x = choose (m + n) m * dpow (m + n) x
  dpow_comp : ∀ {m n x} (_ : n ≠ 0) (_ : x ∈ I),
    dpow m (dpow n x) = uniformBell m n * dpow (m * n) x

qualifications: WittVector.isocrystal_classification assumes finrank exactly one; it does not supply Dieudonne-Manin in all ranks.
The reductive-group and torus predicates are built. Their rational Newton, sigma-conjugacy, local-global cohomology and Shimura interfaces are separate contracts.

The dominant-chamber uniqueness result is for a finite reduced crystallographic root system with the flipped pairing reduced and strictly ordered coefficients. The central torus and rational coroot cone adapters remain N05.
TauCeti.posRootCone in RootSystem/Positive.lean uses integral nonnegative coefficients. It does not by itself supply the rational dominance cone used here.
The abelian-variety and finite-surjective isogeny carriers are reused; the relative universal family, rational Hom tensor functor and isogeny torsors are additional contracts.
A divided-power structure is not a PD envelope, log site, convergent isocrystal or crystalline comparison theorem.
Proposed API wrappers on library items are not additional claims that their names or full contracts are implemented.

The pinned Coxeter Bruhat file gives the order and a partial-order structure. It explicitly does not prove the full converse subword theorem there. No affine Iwahori–Weyl realization is inferred from its name.
Mathlib Burnside counts fixed points of any finite group action. E13 derives the finite coset derangement corollary; it is not claimed under a guessed library name.

items.name: Stembridge positive-coroot step
items.statement: If dominant integral lambda<mu in coroot dominance, there is a positive coroot alpha∨ such that lambda+alpha∨ is dominant and <=mu.
items.note: Full Waldspurger proof in Rapoport00 Lemma2.3 reread; its two root-sum/sign leaves are in the pinned Mathlib.
proofSteps: Write mu-lambda=sum n_i a_i with n_i nonnegative integers and not all0. The finite set X of positive roots beta=sum m_i a_i with every m_i<=n_i is nonempty, since a simple root with n_i>0 is eligible.
Choose a maximal beta in X under coefficientwise order. For each simple root a_i, either beta+a_i is not a root or m_i=n_i.
In the first case, L20 and positivity (beta!=-a_i) imply the relevant simple coroot pairing of beta is >=0; add the nonnegative pairing of lambda.
In the second case write lambda+beta=mu-sum_(j!=i)(n_j-m_j)a_j. L21 makes every subtracted off-diagonal pairing nonpositive, hence the resulting pairing is >=0.
Thus lambda+beta is dominant and <=mu. Apply the same proof to the dual root pairing for coroot dominance.
acceptance: If dominant integral lambda<mu in coroot dominance, there is a positive coroot alpha∨ such that lambda+alpha∨ is dominant and <=mu.
For PGL_2 with coroot2 and lambda=0,mu=2, the positive-coroot step reaches mu; mu=1 is outside the integral-order hypothesis.
